transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thanks for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time with this... I guess I'm just here because I've been feeling a little, well, off. 

Most days I wake up and it already feels like... like there's this heavy, gray weight sitting on me, you know? I mean, I still get up and go to work with the landscaping crew, I always get the job done. I don't want you to think I'm slacking or complaining or anything. But even when I'm out there working with the guys, or back home around my kids, I just can't seem to shake this... this low, hollow feeling. It's like I'm just going through the motions every day. I try really hard to hide it so I don't bring anyone else down, but... yeah. 

Does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing I should be coming in for?
How long have you been feeling this low, hollow feeling?

Well, it's... it's been a while, honestly. I hope I haven't let it go on too long before getting help. I'd say it's been about three years and... maybe three months? Give or take. 

It started right around the time our groundskeeping contract changed at work. They shifted our schedule, and suddenly these really long days just sort of... took over my life. I mean, I don't mind hard work, I really don't! I'm happy to do whatever they need me to do. But I think that's when this feeling really settled in and just hasn't left. Is it normal for a schedule change to mess with a person for that long? I feel a little silly letting it get to me like this.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like before this feeling started?

Well, um... I guess I still do some of those things. I try to, anyway. Like, I used to really love going fishing with my boys on the weekends. And I still take them! I make sure we go, because I want them to have a good time. But... I don't know, maybe I'm just getting older, but I don't really get that same... spark out of it anymore. 

It's not that I hate it or anything! I don't want you to think I'm ignoring my kids or being a bad dad. I'm out there baiting hooks and everything. It's just... I guess I'm mostly doing it for them now. I don't really feel much of anything while we're out there. Is that... does that sound like what you're asking about? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in?

Um... honestly? Not really. I mean, I try to find the good in things, I really do. I don't want to sound like a complainer who just sits around moping all the time. But... no. Even watching a ballgame on TV or having a beer after work, it all just feels sort of... flat. 

I mean, I still do those things because that's what you're supposed to do, right? You're supposed to relax and have a hobby. But I don't really get any joy out of it anymore. It's just something to pass the time before I have to go back to sleep and start the whole thing over again. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds awful. I really should be more grateful for the things I have. Is it okay that I don't really have a good answer for that one?
Do you ever feel like you're looking forward to something, but when it happens, it doesn't feel as good as you thought it would?

Well, um... I'm trying to think. I want to give you a good answer, but... I don't really know if I experience that. Mostly because... well, to be completely honest, I don't really find myself looking forward to much of anything beforehand, either. 

I hope that doesn't sound too, you know, miserable! I really try not to be a drag to be around. But yeah, I guess since I don't really get that excited feeling before something happens, I don't get that letdown feeling you're talking about. I just sort of wake up and do the work that needs to be done. 

Is... is that an okay way to answer that? I'm sorry if I'm not giving you what you need for your notes. I just don't think I really have that happen to me.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities you used to enjoy?

Well, um... I think we might have just talked about that a little bit, didn't we? About the fishing and the ballgames and stuff? I hope I'm not misunderstanding the question! 

But yeah, I guess... I guess the answer is yes. I just don't really have that drive to do the things I used to like. I still do them, like I said! I'm not just giving up on everything. I really try to keep busy. But the actual interest in doing them... yeah, I suppose that's pretty much gone. 

I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself. I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way. Am I making sense?
Have you experienced any periods of feeling even worse than you do now over the past three years?

Um... let me think about that. I really want to be accurate for you. I don't... I don't think so? 

I mean, it's just been this same sort of flat, heavy feeling for... gosh, for a long time now. It doesn't really dip down into something worse, it just stays right here. I hope that's okay to say. I know some people have these really big crashes, and I don't want it to seem like I'm making a big deal out of nothing since I don't have those. It's just... it's just always this same gray feeling, every day. 

Is that helpful? I'm sorry if that's not the kind of pattern you were looking for. I just don't think there's been a time where it was noticeably worse than it is right now.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns since this feeling started?

Well, um... gosh, I hope I'm being helpful here. I don't really think there's been a big change with either of those things. 

I mean, I still eat my meals. I try to make sure I'm getting enough food so I can do my job, you know? I'm on my feet a lot for work, so I have to keep my strength up. I don't want to be a bother to my crew by slacking off. And with sleep... well, I lay down at night and I get up when the alarm goes off. It's just sort of the same routine it's always been, I guess. 

I hope it's alright that I don't have a more dramatic answer for you. I know you're trying to figure this all out. Am I giving you enough detail, or did you need me to try and track my meals or something for you? I'd be happy to do that if it helps.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from activities that would normally bring you happiness?

Well, um... I guess that sounds a lot like what we were just talking about, right? With the fishing and everything? I hope I'm not getting your questions mixed up or anything. 

I wouldn't say I'm completely unable to feel any pleasure at all. I really don't want to sound ungrateful, or like I'm just totally miserable to be around! If one of the guys on the crew tells a good joke while we're laying mulch, I still laugh. Or if it's a really nice, cool morning out on the grounds, I can appreciate it. It's not like I'm completely numb to every good thing. I can still crack a smile when something nice happens. 

It's just... I guess the feeling doesn't really stay with me very long, or I don't get excited about it beforehand like I used to. But I definitely wouldn't say I'm totally unable to feel it. 

Does that make sense? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture here. I hope I'm explaining it okay for you.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from activities that would normally bring you happiness most of the time?

Oh, I see... I'm sorry, I probably wasn't very clear just a second ago. That's my fault. 

Um, "most of the time"... no, I don't think I'd say that. I really try hard to keep a good attitude, you know? I don't want to be a downer for the rest of the guys on the crew. So, even if I'm feeling a little flat, I still make an effort to enjoy the day. It's not like I'm just... miserable from morning till night. I still try to find the good in things as much as I can. 

I hope it's okay that I don't fit that exactly. I know you're trying to check off the right boxes for this. I'm really trying to give you the best picture I can without making myself sound worse than I am... did that answer what you were asking?
Has this low, hollow feeling lasted for at least two years?

Well, um... gosh, two years? I hope I'm not being difficult, but it's actually been a bit longer than that. I'm sorry if that complicates things for you. 

I'd say it's been... maybe closer to three years? Three years and a few months, I think. It kind of started back when the groundskeeping contract we have changed up our whole schedule. The days got a lot longer, and it just sort of... took over my life, I guess. I didn't want to complain to the boss or anything, because I'm grateful to have the work, you know? But that's when this feeling really seemed to settle in. 

I hope it's alright that it's been going on that long. I probably should have come in sooner so you wouldn't have to deal with such a backlog of it, huh? Is that the kind of timeframe you were looking for?
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities that used to bring you pleasure, to the point where you don't enjoy them at all?

Oh, um... I feel like I might be making this harder for you, and I'm really sorry if I am. I know this sounds a whole lot like what you asked just a minute ago. I hope I'm not sounding like a broken record or frustrating you. 

But, um, no... not to the point where I don't enjoy them *at all*. I'd hate for you to think I've just completely given up on everything. Like I was saying before, I still try to get out there and do things, and I can still get a little something out of it while it's happening. It's definitely not a total zero. I really do try to keep up with my life so I'm not just, you know, a lump on the couch bringing everybody down. 

I just... I don't want to paint it as worse than it actually is. I still have things I care about and try to enjoy. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering it right for you this time.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from almost all activities most of the day?

Oh, gosh, I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm making you repeat yourself. I really hope I'm not being difficult or wasting your time with all this. 

Um, to answer your question... no, not almost all activities, and definitely not most of the day. I'd feel terrible if I let things get that bad. I mean, I still get up, I go to work, I talk with the guys on the crew... I can still find little moments in the day that are okay. It's not like I'm just walking around like a zombie all day long. I really try to push through and be present, you know? 

I just... I don't want you to think I'm completely incapable of enjoying anything. I'm really trying my best to hold it together. I hope that's the kind of answer you need? I'm sorry if I'm not explaining it very well.
Has this low, hollow feeling been present for most of every day?

Well, um... yeah, I guess it is. I hope it's okay to admit that. I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining or, you know, not trying hard enough. 

But... yeah, most days, I wake up and it already feels like there's this heavy, gray weight sitting right on me. I try to push it aside, I really do. But even when I'm out working with the crew, or... or when I'm at home around my kids, I just can't seem to shake that low, hollow feeling. It's like I'm just going through the motions, no matter what I'm doing. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible dad or a bad worker. I really am trying my best to be present for everyone. It's just... it's kind of always there in the background most of the day. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from things that would normally bring you happiness, such as spending time with your family or doing activities you used to enjoy?

Oh, geez, I... I feel terrible, I must be doing a really bad job of explaining things today. I'm so sorry if I'm making you ask the same sort of thing over and over. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or talk in circles. 

But, um... no. No, I can definitely still feel happiness, especially with my family. I mean, my kids, they mean the world to me. If I couldn't feel anything around them, I... well, I'd feel like a pretty awful dad. I really don't want you to think I'm totally numb to the people I love. 

Even if I've got that heavy feeling going on in the background, if we're having dinner or I'm just watching the kids out in the yard, I can still feel good about it. I still enjoy them, and I still get happiness from those moments. I really hope that's a better answer for you? I'm just trying to make sure I don't paint the wrong picture and make myself sound worse than I am. Am I doing okay with these questions?
Do you feel like this low, hollow feeling is mild, or is it interfering with your daily life in a more significant way?

Oh, wow, um... I really hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than it is. I know there are people out there with real problems, and I don't want to sound like I'm whining. I really try to keep things running smoothly, I promise I do. 

But... well, I guess it is starting to get in the way a bit. I feel so embarrassed even admitting this, because I've always prided myself on being reliable. But lately... I don't know, I've just been missing some details when I'm planning out the landscaping jobs, and I've been falling behind on the paperwork for the crew. I hate that I'm letting that slip. 

And, um, outside of work, I used to help organize the community garden and these little music gatherings we'd have. But lately, I've just been avoiding them. It's awful, because people used to count on me for that stuff, and now they're having to step in and cover for me. I feel like such a letdown. I really am trying to get back on track, though. I don't want you to think I'm just giving up. Is... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm not oversharing.
Do you feel like this low, hollow feeling is significantly impacting your ability to function in your daily life?

Oh, gosh, I... I feel like I'm just repeating myself, and I'm really sorry if I'm not giving you the exact answer you need. I hope you don't mind me just trying to explain it again. 

I don't know if I'd say it's... significantly impacting everything. I mean, I'm still getting out of bed, I'm still showing up for work, I'm still feeding the kids. I'm really trying my hardest to keep it all together so nobody else has to pick up my slack. I don't want to sound like I'm completely falling apart or anything like that. 

It's just... like I said, I'm missing some details at work and avoiding the community garden stuff. But I'm still functioning, you know? I'm still getting the absolute necessities done. I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, or like I'm not trying. Am I... am I answering the question right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture without sounding like a complainer.
Would you say that your low, hollow feeling is moderately severe, or is it more mild?

Oh, geez, I... I really don't want to make a mountain out of a molehill here. I know I keep saying that, and I'm sorry if it's annoying. I just... I don't want to come across like I'm making excuses for myself. 

I guess... well, it feels pretty heavy. Maybe... maybe more on the severe side? I mean, it's always there, just this constant weight pulling me down, even when I'm trying my absolute hardest to push through it. It takes so much energy just to get through the day sometimes. But I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around wallowing in it! I really am trying to keep up with everything. 

Does that... does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too dramatic. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea of how it feels.
Has this low, hollow feeling lasted for more than two years?

Oh, um... yes. It has. I'm really sorry, I know I probably should have said something to a doctor way before now, or just figured out how to snap out of it on my own. I don't want you to think I haven't been trying to fix it myself, because I really have. 

If I'm being completely honest, it's been... gosh, maybe a little over three years? Like three years and three months, give or take. It all started right around the time our groundskeeping contract changed at work. They shifted our schedule, and... well, the longer days just sort of took over my life. I really tried to just put my head down and work through it, I promise I did. I didn't want to complain to the boss or be a burden to the rest of the crew. But that's when this feeling started, and it just... never really lifted. 

Is it awful that I let it go on that long without getting help? I hope you don't think less of me for not handling it better. I just kept thinking I could push through it if I tried harder.
